papers.title_en: EventSSM: Causal Spatial-State Modelling for Asynchronous Events Event-Depth Estimation
papers.authors: Sadiq O. Macaulay, Dipon Ghosh, Hadfield Simon
papers.evidence: 从异步事件流进行度量深度估计
papers.tldr: 事件相机输出异步亮度变化，但度量深度监督通常只在稀疏参考时刻可得，聚合成帧会丢失细粒度时间结构。EventSSM 提出因果空间状态框架，用按时间顺序的事件包更新循环记忆来做事件关联的度量深度估计。为连接异步预测与帧时刻监督，预测的事件深度借助标定位姿做几何变换，并在参考时刻可微渲染。基准测试显示其在多项深度误差指标上优于已有事件深度方法，消融验证了各组件有效性。
papers.abstract_en: Event cameras report asynchronous brightness changes, yet metric-depth supervision is typically available only at sparsely sampled reference timestamps. Aggregating events into frame-like representations simplifies learning but can obscure the fine-grained temporal structure of the original event stream. We introduce EventSSM, a causal spatial-state framework for event-associated metric-depth estimation using a recurrent memory updated by chronological event packets. To bridge asynchronous predictions and frame-time supervision, predicted event depths are geometrically transported using calibrated camera poses and differentiably rendered at reference timestamps. Benchmark evaluations demonstrate improvements over established event-depth methods across multiple depth-error measures. Controlled ablations further examine cross-modal initialization, temporal recurrence, individual state, readout, and supervision components, and packet subdivision. Together, these findings establish EventSSM as an effective framework for causal event-associated metric-depth estimation, combining persistent spatial context with physically timed state retention.
